name: Do kitchen additions in Glendale or Pasadena require a permit?

mainEntity.name: Do kitchen additions in Glendale or Pasadena require a permit?
mainEntity.text: Do kitchen additions in Glendale or Pasadena require a permit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, kitchen additions generally require permits in Glendale and Pasadena because they affect building structure, utility systems, or usable floor area. Even when a project looks straightforward, adding square footage, moving plumbing, changing wall openings, or altering load-bearing elements usually triggers permit review. Homeowners should expect building, electrical, plumbing, and possibly mechanical approvals depending on the scope. In some cases, zoning or planning review may also be needed before the building permit stage. The most practical approach is to have a contractor or designer verify the scope early so the plans match the permit pathway. That helps avoid stop-work issues, inspection delays, and redesign costs. This question is underserved because many pages explain permits for small remodels but do not clearly separate those from addition work. A strong answer should tell readers that cosmetic updates may be simpler, but additions almost always need formal approval and inspections before or during construction. Local rules also matter, so the exact permit path can vary by city and by how much of the home is being altered.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. A kitchen addition in Glendale or Pasadena generally requires permits because it changes the home’s structure, footprint, utilities, or both. If the project involves new plumbing, electrical work, walls, openings, foundation work, or added square footage, plan review and inspections are usually required before construction starts.
